  • Parameter types and binding names

Parameter types and binding names

Parameter type (param_type)

The parameters of each node are divided into two categories:

init_params (initialization parameters) run_params (operation parameters)

Features

loads once, usually heavier (model files, configuration files, etc.)

Can be different per run, usually lighter (thresholds, switches, etc.)

When will

take effect? When

calls initial_node() When

calls activate_node() or run_graph()

Typical content

Model file path, network structure configuration, weight file

Confidence threshold, maximum number of detections, ROI area

Update cost

High: Node needs to be reinitialized after changes

Low: It can be changed at any time and it will take effect next time it is run.

Usage in code

from atom_sdk import NodeParamUpdate

# Set initialization parameters(model file)
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        node_id,
        "model",       # Parameter name,from get_node_info_in_graph Check
        "init_params", # Fixed writing method
        Path("/models/detector.bin"),  # Path Object automatically uploaded
    )
)

# Set operating parameters(threshold)
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        node_id,
        "confidence_threshold",
        "run_params",  # Fixed writing method
        0.85,
    )
)

param_type has only two legal values: "init_params" and "run_params". An error will not be reported if written incorrectly, but the parameters will not take effect.

Binding name (binding_name)

What is a binding name

The binding name is the externally exposed name of the node port or parameter, which is the interface for communication between the child graph and the parent graph.

In the subgraph node (GraphNode), if the port inside the subgraph is set with a binding name, it can be:

  • Other nodes in the parent graph are connected to

  • Access by name at runtime via RuntimeService

If no binding name is set, the port is only visible inside the subgraph and cannot be directly accessed from the outside.

Port name vs Binding name

Concept Explanation Example

origin_name / port name

The original port or parameter name inside the node

"output_image"

binding_name

Exposed name (can be different)

"rgb_frame"

The purpose of setting the binding name is to provide a more meaningful interface name to the outside world without exposing internal implementation details.

Binding type (binding_type)

value description

"inputs"

Enter the binding name of the port

"outputs"

Binding name of the output port

"init_params"

Binding name of initialization parameter

"run_params"

Binding name of running parameters

Example of setting a binding name

from atom_sdk import SubGraphBindingUpdate

# Set the binding name for the output port of the subgraph internal node
client.graph_node.set_binding_name(
    SubGraphBindingUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        graph_node_id,
        inner_node_id,
        "outputs",
        "output_image",    # The port name inside the node
        "processed_frame", # External binding name
    )
)

# Unbind(Pass empty string)
client.graph_node.set_binding_name(
    SubGraphBindingUpdate(
        "my_graph",
        graph_node_id,
        inner_node_id,
        "outputs",
        "output_image",
        "",  # An empty string indicates unbinding
    )
)

What binding names are used for in RuntimeService

The shared parameter interface of RuntimeService accesses the parameters of the graph through the binding name:

from atom_sdk import BindingRef, RuntimeParamsUpdate

# Read the binding metainformation of the graph
meta = client.runtime.get_meta_info("my_graph")
print("Meta information request status:", meta["status"])
# Return {"sharedParams": [...], "runtimeParams": [...]}
# Each parameter has "bindingName" Field

# Set shared parameters in batches by binding name
client.runtime.set_shared_params(
    RuntimeParamsUpdate("my_graph", {
        "model_path": "/models/new_model.bin",  # bindingName → value
        "max_detection": 10,
    })
)

client.runtime.set_run_params(RuntimeParamsUpdate("my_graph", {"threshold": 0.7}))

# Read output value by binding name
output_value = client.runtime.get_binded_output_value(
    BindingRef("my_graph", "processed_frame")  # bindingName
)

How to check what ports and parameters a node has

Use get_node_info_in_graph to see the full definition of a node:

from atom_sdk import NodeRef

info = client.node.get_node_info_in_graph(NodeRef("my_graph", node_id))

# View init_params
for param in info["nodeInfo"].get("initParams", []):
    print(f"  init_params: {param['name']} ({param['type']})")

# View run_params
for param in info["nodeInfo"].get("runParams", []):
    print(f"  run_params: {param['name']} ({param['type']})")

# View input ports
for port in info["nodeInfo"].get("inputs", []):
    print(f"  input: {port['name']}")

# View output port
for port in info["nodeInfo"].get("outputs", []):
    print(f"  output: {port['name']}")
